intro: What was going on when something else happened: estaba plus gerund, cuando and mientras.
p.estaba.consejo: With a gerund it says what was in progress: «estaba leyendo». It is the same for yo and él.
p.estabas.consejo: To ask a friend: «¿Qué estabas haciendo?». It ends in -s, like all tú forms.
p.haciendo.consejo: The c sounds «th» in Spain: a-THYEN-do. With «estar»: «¿qué estás haciendo?».
p.durmiendo.consejo: In dormir, the o changes to u in the gerund: «durmiendo», not «dormiendo».
p.leyendo.consejo: Between vowels, the i becomes y: «leyendo», not «leiendo». It is the same in «oyendo».
p.mientras.consejo: It joins two actions happening at the same time: «mientras duermes, yo trabajo». It is written with -ie-.
p.de repente.consejo: It announces an unexpected event and usually goes with the indefinido: «de repente sonó el teléfono».
p.entonces.consejo: It moves the story forward: «entonces abrí la puerta». The c sounds «th» in Spain.
p.luego.consejo: It orders actions: first one, «luego» the other. You can also say «después».
p.sonó.consejo: The accent is on the o. It is the phone verb: «sonó el teléfono». In the present the o becomes ue: «suena».
p.oí.consejo: It has an accent to separate the vowels: o-Í. It is a single event: «oí un ruido».
p.el teléfono.consejo: The accent marks the stressed syllable: te-LÉ-fo-no. «El móvil» is also used for the mobile phone.
p.la ducha.consejo: You say «estar en la ducha» and «darse una ducha». The ch sounds as in «chocolate».
p.otra vez.consejo: It is two words: «otra vez». The z sounds «th» and the v sounds «b».
b1.texto:
**Estar in the imperfect + gerund** tells an action **in progress** at a moment in the past.

- A las diez **estaba durmiendo**.
- ¿Qué **estabas haciendo**?
- **Estaba durmiendo** cuando **llamaste**. (The indefinido tells the event that interrupts.)

Forms of **estar**: **estaba, estabas, estaba, estábamos, estabais, estaban**. **Estabais** is used mainly in Spain.

**Mientras** joins two simultaneous actions: **Mientras tú dormías, yo trabajaba.**

Gerunds: **-ar → -ando**, **-er / -ir → -iendo**. If there is a vowel before, the i becomes y: **leer → leyendo**. Common irregulars: **durmiendo, pidiendo, diciendo, oyendo, yendo**.

To order a story: **de repente, entonces, luego, al final**.
b2.f3.texto: I did not hear the phone.
b2.f5.texto: I was in the shower when it rang again.
b2.f6.texto: While you were sleeping, I was working.
b2.f7.texto: I will call you again later.
b3.titulo: Actions in progress and story signals
b4.texto:
The recipe is short:

- **estaba / estabas / estaba / estábamos / estabais / estaban**
- + **gerund**: **hablando, comiendo, viviendo**

When to use it:

- To say **what was happening**: **Estaba leyendo.**
- To present the **background** of an event: **Estaba leyendo cuando sonó el teléfono.**
- For two actions **at the same time**: **Mientras leía, mi padre cocinaba.**

You can also say **¿Qué hacías?**: it means almost the same, but **estar + gerund** highlights the moment in progress.

The pronoun can go before **estaba** or attached to the gerund: **Me estaba duchando / Estaba duchándome.**
b4.e0.texto: My neighbours were having dinner in the garden.
b4.e2.texto: Then I put down the book and ran to the door.
b5.f0.texto: I was reading by the window of the living room.
b5.f1.texto: The rain fell on the glass with a soft noise.
b5.f2.texto: My cat slept peacefully on top of a blue blanket.
b5.f3.texto: The water was boiling slowly in the kitchen.
b5.f4.texto: A soft music came from the wet street.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly the phone rang in the dark hallway of the house.
b5.f6.texto: Then I left the book open on the small table.
b5.f7.texto: Then I walked slowly towards that distant sound.
b5.f8.texto: My heart beat very fast in the silence.
b5.f9.texto: At last I heard the cheerful voice of my sister.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Leído» is the participle: «he leído». With «estaba» the gerund goes.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Well done! Between vowels the i becomes y: leyendo.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That form does not exist: the i between vowels is written y.
b6.pregunta: Which gerund of leer completes the sentence?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It announces something unexpected, not two simultaneous actions.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It moves the story forward: one action after another.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Mientras» means «at the same time as».
b7.pregunta: Which word joins two simultaneous actions?
b8.frase: No oí el teléfono porque estaba durmiendo
b8.traduccion: I did not hear the phone because I was sleeping
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done: the call is a single event that interrupts.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It would turn the call into background too; the interrupting event is missing.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is present: the story is in the past.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «estaba» + gerund shows dinner in progress.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It tells a finished event, not an action in progress.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is future: it has not happened yet.
b10.pregunta: Which sentence presents an action in progress?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «What were you doing?» (tú)
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Hecho» is the participle: «he hecho». Here a gerund goes.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That form does not exist: -er verbs form the gerund with -iendo.
b12.pregunta: Which gerund of hacer completes the question?
p.llamé.consejo: The accent marks the past for yo: «llamo» is now.
p.dormías.consejo: The accent on í breaks the vowels: dor-MÍ-as.
p.corrí.consejo: The accent shows the past for yo: «corro» is now.
p.dormía.consejo: The accent on í splits the vowels: dor-MÍ-a.
p.hervía.consejo: The h is silent: «hervía» sounds like er-BI-a.
p.lentamente.consejo: Adverbs ending in -mente come from an adjective: «lento» gives «lentamente».
p.deprisa.consejo: Here the stress falls on PRI: de-PRI-sa.
p.llegaste.consejo: The ll sounds like y: ye-GAS-te.
